title: I Finally Read the Classics I've Been Pretending to Have Read
creator: Ellie Reads
description:
Twelve classics, three months, a lot of tea. Which ones were worth it and which ones I'd only recommend to my enemies.

The full list is pinned in the comments.
Goodreads: ellie_reads

sentences.t: Okay, confession time, for years I have nodded along when people talk about certain books that I have absolutely never read.
So this summer I made a list of twelve of them, and I read them all, and I have opinions.
Let's start with the one I was most scared of, which is Middlemarch.
It's about eight hundred pages, and I genuinely thought I would quit by chapter three.
And reader, I loved it.
It's basically a whole town's worth of people making bad decisions about who to marry, and it is so much funnier than anyone told me.
Dorothea is a hero, Casaubon is the worst man in literature, and I will be taking no questions.
Next, Moby-Dick, and I'm sorry, but I need to be honest here.
There's a great forty-page novel inside this book, and then there's a very long manual about whales.
I learned more about whale blubber than I ever wanted to know, and I still don't know why the chapter on the color white exists.
Then Jane Eyre, which was a delight, a gothic romance with a surprisingly angry heroine, which I respect.
And Crime and Punishment, which stressed me out so much I had to read it in daylight.
Real question, though, when's the last time you actually finished a nonfiction book?
Because for me, doing this project, I realized all my reading time had gone to novels, and my to-be-read pile of nonfiction was just collecting dust.
That's where today's sponsor, Blinkist, comes in.
Blinkist takes the key ideas from over seven thousand nonfiction books and turns them into fifteen-minute reads or listens.
I've been using it on my walk to work to figure out which books are worth reading in full, and which ones I'm happy just knowing the main idea of.
Go to blinkist.com/ellie, and the first hundred people get twenty-five percent off Blinkist Premium.
Okay, back to the classics, because I saved the most divisive ones for last.
Wuthering Heights.
Everyone told me it's a love story, and it is not a love story, it's two families ruining each other across two generations on a very windy hill.
I didn't like a single person in it, and I could not put it down, so I guess that's a win?
The Great Gatsby, which is short, beautiful, and I get why every English teacher loves it.
Pride and Prejudice, which I'd technically seen four adaptations of, so that one felt like cheating.
Then Anna Karenina, which I'll do a whole separate video on because I have too many feelings about Levin and his farming chapters.
And the one I actually didn't finish was Ulysses.
I made it about two hundred pages in, and then I accepted that this book and I are not meant to be.
Maybe next summer, maybe never.
So, my ranking, Middlemarch at the top, Jane Eyre second, and Moby-Dick somewhere near the bottom with the whales.
Tell me which classic you secretly haven't read, it's a safe space, nobody here is judging.
I'll see you next week with my autumn reading list.
